# `execution/disk-cleaner.ts`

Utilities for scanning and removing orphaned worktrees, stale preview artefacts, and stale temporary directories. The module provides safe, validated deletion backed by path-traversal protection and active-task awareness.

## Types & Interfaces

### `DiskItemType`

A type alias representing the category of a disk item.

```ts
import type { DiskItemType } from './execution/disk-cleaner';
```

---

### `DiskItem`

Represents a single filesystem candidate identified for cleanup.

```ts
import type { DiskItem } from './execution/disk-cleaner';
```

| Member | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | `string` | Absolute path on disk |
| `type` | `DiskItemType` | Category of the item |
| `sizeBytes` | `number` | Estimated size in bytes |
| `createdAt` | `Date` | Directory creation timestamp |
| `reason` | `string` | Human-readable reason why this item is considered orphaned/stale |

---

### `CleanResult`

Summarises the outcome of a `clean()` call.

```ts
import type { CleanResult } from './execution/disk-cleaner';
```

| Member | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `freedBytes` | `number` | Total bytes reclaimed across all removed items |
| `removedCount` | `number` | Number of items successfully deleted |
| `errors` | `string[]` | Per-item error messages for any deletions that failed |

## Functions

### `dirSizeBytes`

```ts
import { dirSizeBytes } from './execution/disk-cleaner';

async function dirSizeBytes(dirPath: string): Promise<number>
```

Recursively computes the total size of a directory in bytes. Falls back to `0` on any error (e.g. permission denied).

#### Parameters

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `dirPath` | `string` | Path to the directory to measure |

#### Returns

`Promise<number>` — Total size of the directory tree in bytes, or `0` on error.

#### Example

```ts
const bytes = await dirSizeBytes('/tmp/hive-worktrees/hive-HIVE-20260222-abc123');
console.log(`Directory is ${bytes} bytes`);
```

---

### `parseGitWorktreeList`

```ts
import { parseGitWorktreeList } from './execution/disk-cleaner';

function parseGitWorktreeList(output: string): string[]
```

Parses the output of `git worktree list --porcelain` and returns an array of worktree paths listed by git.

#### Parameters

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `output` | `string` | Raw stdout from `git worktree list --porcelain` |

#### Returns

`string[]` — Ordered list of absolute worktree paths extracted from the porcelain output.

#### Example

```ts
const raw = `
worktree /tmp/hive-worktrees/hive-HIVE-20260222-abc123
HEAD abc123
branch refs/heads/feature-x

worktree /bare
HEAD def456
bare
`.trim();

const paths = parseGitWorktreeList(raw);
// => ['/tmp/hive-worktrees/hive-HIVE-20260222-abc123', '/bare']
```

### `getActiveTaskIds`

```ts
import { getActiveTaskIds } from './execution/disk-cleaner';

async function getActiveTaskIds(): Promise<Set<string>>
```

Fetches the set of task IDs that are currently active — i.e. not in a terminal state. Terminal states are: `completed`, `failed`, `cancelled`.

#### Parameters

None.

#### Returns

`Promise<Set<string>>` — A set of active task ID strings.

#### Example

```ts
const activeIds = await getActiveTaskIds();
if (activeIds.has('HIVE-20260222-abc123')) {
  console.log('Task is still running');
}
```

### `scan`

```ts
import { scan } from './execution/disk-cleaner';

async function scan(): Promise<DiskItem[]>
```

Scans the filesystem for orphan worktrees, stale preview artefacts, and stale temp directories. Returns a structured list of candidates for cleanup. Does not delete anything.

#### Parameters

None.

#### Returns

`Promise<DiskItem[]>` — List of [`DiskItem`](#diskitem) objects representing cleanup candidates.

#### Example

```ts
const candidates = await scan();
for (const item of candidates) {
  console.log(`${item.path} (${item.sizeBytes} bytes) — ${item.reason}`);
}
```

### `validatePaths`

```ts
import { validatePaths } from './execution/disk-cleaner';

async function validatePaths(paths: string[]): Promise<void>
```

Validates that every path to be deleted satisfies all of the following conditions:

1. Is an absolute path.
2. Does not contain path-traversal sequences after normalisation.
3. Is strictly inside `WORKTREE_BASE` after symlink resolution.

Symlinks are resolved via `realpath()` before the containment check, preventing symlink-based escape attempts. Throws on the first invalid path encountered.

#### Parameters

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `paths` | `string[]` | List of absolute paths to validate before deletion |

#### Returns

`Promise<void>` — Resolves if all paths are valid; throws an error on the first violation.

#### Example

```ts
try {
  await validatePaths(['/tmp/hive-worktrees/hive-HIVE-20260222-abc123']);
  console.log('All paths are safe to delete');
} catch (err) {
  console.error('Unsafe path detected:', err);
}
```

---

### `clean`

```ts
import { clean } from './execution/disk-cleaner';

async function clean(paths: string[]): Promise<CleanResult>
```

Deletes the specified paths from disk. Each path is validated before deletion to prevent path-traversal attacks. Collects and returns per-item errors rather than halting on the first failure.

#### Parameters

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `paths` | `string[]` | List of absolute paths to remove |

#### Returns

`Promise<CleanResult>` — A [`CleanResult`](#cleanresult) containing the number of freed bytes, successfully removed item count, and any per-item error messages.

#### Example

```ts
const candidates = await scan();
const pathsToDelete = candidates.map((item) => item.path);

const result = await clean(pathsToDelete);

console.log(`Freed ${result.freedBytes} bytes across ${result.removedCount} items`);

if (result.errors.length > 0) {
  console.warn('Some items could not be removed:');
  result.errors.forEach((e) => console.warn(' -', e));
}
```

---

## Notes

> **`extractTaskId`** is an internal helper and is **not exported** from the module. It checks whether a directory name contains a `HIVE-YYYYMMDD-xxxxxxxx` token that does not correspond to an active task ID, returning the token if found or `null` if ownership cannot be determined. Unrecognised directories are conservatively retained.
